newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's NH in joint venture with France's Accor.
newsitem.headline: Spain's NH in joint venture with France's Accor.

text.p: Spanish hotel chain NH Hoteles announced on Tuesday a 50-50 joint venture with its French counterpart Accord to set up a chain of second-tier hotels under the name Ibis.
The two firms have initiated Desarrollo y Explotacion de Hotels, with start-up capital of two billion pesetas.
It plans to open its first six or seven hotels within one year, and to have between 60 and 70 hotels in six or seven years.
NH hotels, 62 percent-owned by Corporacion Financiera Reunida (Cofir) denied imminent plans for public listing.
In summer 1996 the company had said it was considering flotation by October.
In the meantime in December, Italian financier Carlo De Benedetti sold his 48.05 percent majority stake in Cofir to around 70 European institutional investors.
NH hotels made 1996 net profit of around 920 million pesetas after 800 million pesetas in 1995. It owns 70 hotels in around 22 cities.
